content.text: All preferred elements are present across §§ 24.1–24.4, with no change-of-control trigger elsewhere in the document.

input.quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.
input.rationale: Section 24 meets our preferred position in full. 24.1 lets Customer assign to an Affiliate or to a merger/acquisition/asset-sale successor without Vendor's consent (notice only, no consent condition). 24.2 bars Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, with the reasonableness standard running in our favour, and bars transfer to a direct Customer competitor. 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on Customer's change of control, and 13.3 carries the same permission through to licence transfers. Searches for "change of control" and "assign" surface no other Vendor exit or re-pricing trigger; 9.2 is an ordinary insolvency clause and expressly excludes lawful reorganizations. Minor sub-element note only (not a deviation): the competitor bar in 24.2 is framed as "without Customer's consent" rather than absolute, which adds nothing adverse given 24.2 already conditions every Vendor assignment on our consent. No redline proposed.
